name: CA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Mark DeSaulnier running with a large cash advantage
Prediction markets price DeSaulnier near certain
No competitive polling or expert ratings signal a race
model.rationale: DeSaulnier holds a D+18 seat, has out-raised Jeff Frese substantially, and markets price his win at roughly 96%. With no polls or ratings suggesting competition, the fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit win.
model.watch: A surprise surge in Republican turnout or outside spending against DeSaulnier could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mark DeSaulnier, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Bay Area district that leans Democratic by about 18 points. He advanced to the general election and has raised over $560,000 with nearly $590,000 on hand, while Republican Jeff Frese reports little financial activity and no outside support. No public polls or expert ratings track this race, and prediction markets give DeSaulnier roughly a 96% chance of winning.

The combination of a heavily Democratic electorate, incumbency, and a large fundraising edge makes this one of the safest House seats on the ballot. The realistic question is the size of the margin, not the winner.
